claim: ConsumerLab testing of 31 vitamin D supplements found two products containing nearly twice the labeled amount of vitamin D, both well above the tolerable upper intake level of 4,000 IU.
stance_target: Vitamin D overdosing from supplements is a real documented risk
scope_conditions: 31 vitamin D supplements tested (19 CL-selected + 12 voluntary certification), 2024-2026
quoted_support: Among the vitamin D-containing supplements that CL selected for testing, two were found to contain nearly twice the vitamin D they listed – putting both way over the tolerable upper intake level for vitamin D.
numbers: 100 mcg (4,000 IU) tolerable upper intake level

claim: Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) is preferred over Vitamin D2 (ergocalciferol) as it raises levels more effectively over time and is less likely to cause erroneously low vitamin D blood test results.
stance_target: Briyo's use of D3 (cholecalciferol) is clinically appropriate and superior to D2
scope_conditions: General clinical evidence summarized by ConsumerLab
quoted_support: Vitamin D2 or D3 will raise your vitamin D level, but D3 is preferable as it may raise levels more effectively over time and is less likely to cause erroneously low vitamin D blood test results.

claim: Taking vitamin D with the largest meal of the day (highest fat/oil content) can increase absorption by as much as 50%.
stance_target: Optimal vitamin D supplement intake timing for best results
quoted_support: Take vitamin D supplements with your biggest meal of the day (the one that contains most fats and oils) as this can increase absorption by as much as 50%!

claim: The optimal target blood level of 25-hydroxyvitamin D is 20-39 ng/mL; levels above 39 ng/mL may increase risk of fractures, falls, sleep problems, and earlier death.
stance_target: Recommended safe dosage range for vitamin D supplementation
quoted_support: A total serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D level of at least 20 ng/mL (equivalent to 50 nmol/L) is considered 'sufficient'... Don't exceed 39 ng/mL. Studies show that people with the highest levels of vitamin D tend to have more bone fractures, fall more frequently, sleep less well, and die sooner than those with lower, but sufficient, levels.

claim: For every 1 ng/mL increase in blood vitamin D level, approximately 100 IU of additional daily vitamin D is required (200 IU for obese individuals), taking 6 weeks to reach peak levels.
stance_target: Dosage guidance for vitamin D supplementation including 2,000 IU doses like Briyo
quoted_support: For every 1 ng/mL increase, you'll need to get an additional 100 IU of vitamin D per day (obese individuals may require double the amount... if your blood level is 18 ng/mL, taking 1,000 IU of vitamin D daily... should get you to about 28 ng/mL. It can take 6 weeks to reach the peak.

claim: No Indian vitamin D brands appear in ConsumerLab's tested product list of 31 supplements (2024-2026); all tested brands are established US, European, or North American supplement companies.
stance_target: Briyo's absence from independent third-party testing by ConsumerLab
quoted_support: Brands tested in this Review are AlgaeCal, Bayer, Biotics Research, Caltrate, Carlson, Doctor's Best, Garden of Life, GNC, Innovixlabs, Kirkland Signature [Costco], Life Extension, Metagenics, Sports Research, Nature Made, Nordic Naturals, New Chapter, NOW, Piping Rock, Pure Encapsulations, Source Naturals, Sports Research, Thorne, VitaCost, and Whole Earth & Sea.
